ai.literal: Even to love is there a shutting bolt? Affectionate ones' sorrowful tears will yield a loud proclamation.
ai.translation: Is there a bolt that can shut up love? The sorrowful tears of affectionate people will loudly proclaim it.
ai.modern: அன்பை மறைத்து வைக்கும் தாழ்ப்பாள் உலகத்தில் உண்டோ? அன்புடையவர்கள் படும் துன்பத்தைக் காணும்போது வடியும் கண்ணீரே அந்த அன்பை ஊரறிய வெளிப்படுத்திவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet asks rhetorically if there is any lock or bolt that can keep love hidden away. The answer is no, because true affection cannot be concealed. When people who love see their loved ones suffer, their sorrowful tears will break out and loudly proclaim the love they hold inside.

ai.literal: love / those without / all / to themselves / they are owners / love / those who possess / bone even / they are owners / to others
ai.translation: Those without love claim everything for themselves. Those with love offer even their own bones to others.
ai.modern: அன்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் எல்லாப் பொருள்களையும் தமக்கே உரியதாகக் கொள்வார்கள். ஆனால் அன்பு உடையவர்கள் தம் உடம்பிலுள்ள எலும்பையும் பிறருக்கு உரியதாக்குவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the selfish nature of the loveless with the boundless generosity of the loving. Those who lack love claim everything for themselves, driven entirely by self-interest. In contrast, those who possess love are so selfless that they consider even their own 'bones'—representing their very body and life—as belonging to others. The word 'என்பு' (bone) powerfully symbolizes the ultimate sacrifice one can make out of love.

ai.literal: With love joined way of life, they say, to the precious soul with bone joined connection.
ai.translation: They say that the precious soul's connection to a body of bone is for the sake of living a life united with love.
ai.modern: அருமையான உயிருக்கு எலும்பால் ஆகிய உடம்போடு பொருந்தியுள்ள உறவு, அன்போடு பொருந்தி வாழ்வதற்கான வழியே என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the fundamental purpose of human existence. The phrase 'ஆருயிர்க்கு என்போடு இயைந்த தொடர்பு' refers to the precious soul taking on a physical body, represented here by its framework of 'என்பு' (bone). The poet states that this union of body and soul is meant for 'அன்போடு இயைந்த வழக்கு', which means a life lived in harmony with love. Thus, the capacity to love is presented as the very reason a soul inhabits a physical form.

ai.literal: Love yields the possession of eagerness; that yields the immeasurable excellence called friendship.
ai.translation: Love yields a deep eagerness to connect with others, and that eagerness yields the boundless excellence called friendship.
ai.modern: அன்பு மற்றவர்களிடம் பழகும் ஆர்வத்தை உருவாக்கும்; அந்த ஆர்வம் நட்பு என்று சொல்லப்படும் அளவற்ற சிறப்பை உருவாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes a chain reaction that begins with love. Love produces an eagerness or deep interest in connecting with others. That eagerness, in turn, yields the boundless excellence known as friendship. The word 'நாடா' literally means 'unmeasured' or 'unsought', indicating that the greatness of such friendship is beyond calculation and comes naturally. Through this progression, the text shows how inner affection expands outward into universal bonds.

ai.literal: Love having experienced abiding way they say in the world joy those who experienced attaining excellence.
ai.translation: They say that the excellence attained by those who experience joy in this world is the natural way of a life settled in love.
ai.modern: இவ்வுலகில் இன்பம் அடைந்தவர்கள் பெறும் சிறப்பானது, அவர்கள் அன்பு கொண்டு பொருந்திய வாழ்க்கையின் இயல்பான பயன் என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects the experience of worldly joy and greatness directly to the possession of love. The phrase 'வையகத்து இன்பு உற்றார் எய்தும் சிறப்பு' refers to the excellence and happiness people achieve in their earthly lives. The poet states that this is simply the natural course or practice ('வழக்கு') of a life that is firmly rooted ('அமர்ந்த') in experiencing love ('அன்பு உற்று'). In essence, true joy and distinction in life are not accidental, but the direct fruits of living a life filled with affection for others.

ai.literal: Only to virtue love is a support, say the ignorant; to valor also that itself is help.
ai.translation: The ignorant say that love is an ally only to virtue; it is also a help to valor.
ai.modern: அன்பு அறத்திற்கு மட்டுமே துணையாகும் என்று அறியாதவர்கள் கூறுவார்கள்; வீரத்திற்கும் அந்த அன்பே துணையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet addresses a common misconception that love is only useful for gentle, righteous deeds. The poet states that those who say this are ignorant, as love is equally the driving force behind valor and bravery. The word 'maṟam' here means valor or fierce courage, which often stems from the love and desire to protect one's family or country. Thus, love is the foundational support for both peaceful virtue and fierce bravery.

ai.literal: Bone that which is without sunlight like will scorch indeed, love that which is without virtue.
ai.translation: Just as the sun scorches a boneless creature, virtue will scorch a loveless creature.
ai.modern: எலும்பு இல்லாத புழுக்களை வெயில் சுட்டெரிப்பது போல, அன்பு இல்லாத உயிர்களை அறம் சுட்டெரிக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a powerful parallel between the physical and moral worlds. A boneless creature, like a worm, has no defense against the scorching heat of the sun and perishes. In the exact same way, a soul without love has no protection, and the very force of virtue or righteousness will scorch and destroy it. The word aṟam here represents the natural moral order, which sustains those with love but acts as a destructive force against those without it.

ai.literal: Love inside without life-living hard-land in dried tree having-sprouted like-that.
ai.translation: Living a life without love in one's heart is like a dried-up tree sprouting leaves in barren land.
ai.modern: நெஞ்சில் அன்பு இல்லாமல் வாழும் வாழ்க்கையானது, வறண்ட பாலைநிலத்தில் உள்ள பட்டுப்போன மரம் தளிர்விட்டதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a life devoid of love to a dead, dried-up tree in a barren desert. Just as a withered tree in hard, waterless soil cannot sprout new leaves, a person without love in their heart cannot truly thrive or experience the vitality of life. The word 'வன்பால்' (hard or barren land) emphasizes the harshness of a loveless environment, while 'வற்றல் மரம்' (dried tree) represents the lifelessness of the soul. The comparison 'தளிர்த்தற்று' (like sprouting) is used ironically to show the absolute impossibility of such a life flourishing.

ai.literal: External limbs all what will do, body's internal organ love to those without?
ai.translation: What good are all the external parts of the body to those who lack love, its internal organ?
ai.modern: உடலின் அகத்து உறுப்பாகிய அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, உடலின் புறத்து உறுப்புகள் எல்லாம் இருந்து என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the physical body with the inner self. It asks what use the external limbs and senses are if a person lacks love. Love is described here as the essential internal organ of the body. Without this inner core of affection, mere physical existence and outward features are meaningless.

ai.literal: Of love the path it is, the seat of life; to those without that, bone skin covered body.
ai.translation: A body is truly the seat of life only when it stands in the path of love. To those without love, it is merely bone covered with skin.
ai.modern: அன்பின் வழியில் வாழ்வதுதான் உண்மையான உயிருள்ள உடம்பாகும். அந்த அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு உடம்பு என்பது வெறும் எலும்பைத் தோலால் போர்த்திய ஒரு கூடு மட்டுமே.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what it truly means to be alive. The compound word 'uyirnilai' (seat of life) refers to a living being, which the text says exists only in the path of love. Without love, a person is not truly alive; their physical form is reduced to a mere mechanical structure of bones covered by skin. The stark contrast highlights that love is the essential animating force of human existence.
